messages:
lina: quick post-launch triage check — we shipped 2026.03.20 and already seeing a few noisy items.

lina: TL;DR: 3 user-facing bugs surfaced (one is reproducible), 2 pilot UX asks, and an embeddings flakiness report. need to decide quick patch vs queue for next sprint. can we align in this thread? :eyes:

aj: saw the embeds flake. repro steps are consistent for long inputs, KV cache misses spike. I pasted a short repro: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embed -d '{"text":"<very long text>"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
returns 500 with `kv_cache_evict` in logs.

sophie: customer tickets: #4123 (major search mismatch), #4127 (ui freeze on mobile), #4130 (embed timeout). #4123 is highest SLA impact — impacted 3 enterprise customers. link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/4123

mike: for the two UX asks from pilot team, they're low scope (copy + one-frame layout tweak) but they're conversion-critical for that cohort. estimate: 1 designer + 2 frontend days.

ben: infra note — if we cut a patch for the embed fix we should canary in eu-west-1 first. rolling patch is fine but watch GPU memory pressure on the pool. also recommend temporary throttling on very long inputs as a mitigation flag.

lina: proposal (quick):
- criteria: customer-impact (SLA), correctness/regression, engineering cost, rollout risk.
- rule: P0/P1 by SLA => patch within 48h. UX asks: if <3 dev-days and tied to revenue/pilot, target a fast follow (3-5 day patch). everything else => next sprint.

aj: quick assessment: #4123 (major search mismatch) is a data handling bug, low risk to patch, ~6 dev hours to fix+test. embed timeout looks trickier (kernel path), estimate 2-3 dev days.

sophie: confirming SLA on #4123 is P1 (enterprise uptime impact), customers want a fix ASAP.

mike: happy to do the 1-day turnaround for the copy/layout. can hand off assets by 10:00 PT tomorrow.

lina: decision then:
- #4123 => patch (assign aj)
- embed timeout => triage into Dedicated queue, attempt mitigation (throttle + canary) now
- mobile UI freeze => quick repro attempt and likely patch if reproducible (sophie to share trace)
- pilot UX asks => include in a small follow-up release if engineering can slot it in within 3 working days, else backlog but prioritized high.

aj: taking #4123. I'll open a PR tonight and aim for RC by tomorrow morning.

ben: will prepare canary config and set throttling rule: `max_input_tokens=20000` for impacted endpoints. will monitor mem and tail latencies.

sophie: uploading mobile traces and steps in the ticket now. if aj needs more, ping me.

mike: sending assets and a quick prototype link: https://figma.com/file/x/pilot-ux

release-bot: New release candidate built: `rc-2026.03.21-1` for channel `patches`. CI: ✅, canary deploy scheduled.

lina: nice. next steps: aj -> PR + QA, ben -> canary + throttle, mike -> assets, sophie -> confirm reproduction. I'll run a 9:30 sync tomorrow if we need a quick go/no-go. everyone ok? :thumbsup:

aj: +1

ben: +1

mike: +1

sophie: +1, will be on the 9:30 sync

lina: copying product/eng-oncall to keep visibility. we’ll update the customer-facing status if the patch goes out.

lina: quick log of decisions for handoff:
- Patch: #4123 (aj) target RC within 12h, deploy canary then roll.
- Mitigation: throttle long embeddings + monitor (ben).
- UX follow-up: include if <=3 dev-days else backlog but flagged high (mike -> assets by 10:00 PT).
- Mobile freeze: Sophie to validate and convert to P1 patch if reprod.

lina: thanks all — please add any objections now, otherwise we'll execute on this plan.
